<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>Circle</title>
  <style>
    *,
    *::before,
    *::after {
      box-sizing: border-box;
      margin: 0;
      padding: 0;
    }
    html,
    body {
      min-height: 100%;
    }
    body {
      min-height: 100dvh;
      display: grid;
      place-items: center;
      padding: 1rem;
      background: #f5f5f5;
      color: #111;
    }
    svg {
      width: min(400px, 100%);
      height: auto;
      aspect-ratio: 1;
      display: block;
    }
    circle {
      fill: currentColor;
    }
    @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
      body {
        background: #111;
        color: #f5f5f5;
      }
    }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <svg viewBox="0 0 400 400" role="img" aria-labelledby="circle-title">
    <title id="circle-title">A solid circle</title>
    <circle cx="200" cy="200" r="200"/>
  </svg>
</body>
</html>

content.text:
I rewrote `0.html` with a cleaner, more robust version of the same page.

Changes made:

- **Layout fix:** Replaced the fixed `100vw`/`100vh` body sizing, which causes a horizontal scrollbar when a vertical one appears and misbehaves on mobile browsers, with `min-height: 100dvh` and a grid centering layout.
- **Responsive SVG:** The circle now scales down on screens narrower than 400px instead of overflowing, while keeping its square aspect ratio.
- **Accessibility:** Added a `role="img"` and an SVG `<title>` so screen readers describe the graphic, and replaced the hash-like page title with a readable one.
- **Styling:** Added `box-sizing: border-box`, an explicit fill via `currentColor`, a light background, and a dark-mode variant so the circle stays visible in both color schemes.
- **Cleanup:** Removed the unused `id` on the SVG.

The visual result is unchanged on desktop: a centered 400px black circle.
